title: The Cold Vector
premise: Ulyana Reyes, the last human technician aboard the automated relay station Meridian-9, has spent six years documenting the quiet collapse of the Halcyon colony below—until a distress signal arrives in a language extinct for two centuries, sent by survivors the corporate fleets believe are dead. To prevent two armed fleets from converging on the station and destroying each other over salvage rights, Ulyana fabricates a quarantine protocol, impersonating an authority that no longer exists. As her lie unravels under scrutiny from both fleet commanders and the colonists themselves, she must choose between exposing the truth—which will ignite war—and preserving it, which means sacrificing her own survival. In the end, she broadcasts the colony's death records to both fleets at once, forcing them to share the guilt of abandonment, and escapes as the station burns, carrying the only honest account anyone will ever have.
about_author: Cyrus Okafor is a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade maintaining remote communications posts before turning to fiction. He writes about isolation, obsolete technology, and the people history forgets to check on.

chapters.title: Six Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She maintains Meridian-9 alone, logging the colony's dwindling transmissions and rationing her own supplies while the automation hums around her. A routine day establishes her rituals, her resentment toward the corporation that forgot her, and her habit of talking to the dead relay logs. Emotional beat: loneliness hardened into competence.

chapters.title: The Signal That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A burst transmission arrives in Old Terran Standard—a legal and linguistic dead language. Decoding it, she finds a distress call from Halcyon's deep shelters: survivors, alive, begging for rescue for two hundred days. Her first instinct is to forward it; her second is fear of what both fleets will do. Emotional beat: hope arriving like an infection.

chapters.title: Two Fleets on the Horizon
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Commander Ilsa Voss of the Corporate Recovery Fleet and Captain Deme Osei of the Independent Convoy, both detecting the signal and racing toward Meridian-9. Each believes the other intends to seize the station and erase evidence of colonial negligence. Emotional beat: suspicion sharpening into inevitability.

chapters.title: Quarantine Protocol Seven
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. With hours before arrival, she fabricates a lethal contagion alert in the extinct language, citing an authority—the old Colonial Health Compact—that legally forbids either fleet from boarding. The lie works because no one alive remembers how to disprove it. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration of becoming the law.

chapters.title: The Commander Who Reads Latin
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Aboard the flagship, Voss grows suspicious: the quarantine documents contain grammatical errors no authentic Compact filing would have. She begins quietly verifying, while her officers push for a boarding action that would trigger war with the Convoy. Emotional beat: the slow tightening of a trap Ulyana built herself.

chapters.title: Voices from the Deep Shelters
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She makes contact with the shelter survivors directly—an elderly linguist named Amara Chen who can still read the old tongue. Chen reveals the colonists were deliberately abandoned by the Corporation, and asks Ulyana not to save them but to testify for them. Emotional beat: the weight of being someone's only witness.

chapters.title: The Price of the Lie
chapters.summary: Osei's POV. The Convoy captain decodes part of the quarantine himself and realizes it's forged—but forging it required someone who knew exactly which records the Corporation destroyed. He suspects Ulyana is a whistleblower, not a saboteur, and sends a covert shuttle. His crew demands he use the truth as a weapon instead. Emotional beat: mercy competing with ambition.

chapters.title: Everything Converges
chapters.summary: All three POVs. Voss's verification confirms the forgery just as Osei's shuttle docks; both fleets maneuver into firing positions above the station. Ulyana must choose: confess and let the fleets fight over the wreckage, or double down on a lie that now requires the survivors' silence forever. Emotional beat: cornered, out of time.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, climax. Instead of defending her lie, she transmits six years of unedited colony death records—starvation logs, ignored pleas, corporate deletion orders—to both fleets simultaneously, then opens every channel so neither side can claim ignorance again. The fleets stand down, shamed into stalemate, while the station's reactor, damaged in the standoff, begins to fail. Emotional beat: truth as detonation.

chapters.title: What the Record Keeps
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, resolution. She evacuates with Chen and the surviving colonists aboard Osei's convoy as Meridian-9 burns behind her, its logs already mirrored across both fleets' archives. Voss faces inquiry; Osei chooses testimony over salvage. Ulyana, finally off-station, begins writing the account we've been reading. Emotional beat: grief transformed into record—justice outside the law, paid for in everything she had.
